questions.q: A hardware or software component that records every key pressed on a keyboard to steal passwords is called a:
questions.solution: Keyloggers capture keystrokes (often as spyware/trojan payloads), exposing passwords and OTPs. A sniffer passively captures network packets instead.
questions.shortcut: Key-strokes recorded = keylogger; network packets read = sniffer.

questions.q: Handouts printed with the '3 slides' layout are popular because:
options: Lines for audience notes appear beside each slide
They include the full speaker notes
questions.solution: The 3-slides-per-page handout prints each slide with ruled lines beside it so the audience can take notes. Speaker notes are NOT included (that is the Notes Pages layout).
questions.shortcut: 3-up = slides + note lines; Notes Pages = slide + your notes.

questions.q: Transistors were used as the basic technology of which generation of computers?
questions.solution: The 2nd generation (1956-63) replaced vacuum tubes with transistors, making computers smaller, faster and more reliable. 1st = vacuum tubes, 3rd = ICs, 4th = microprocessors.
questions.shortcut: Generation ladder: Vacuum -> Transistor -> IC -> Microprocessor -> AI. Transistor is the 2nd rung.

questions.q: Which chart type is best suited to show the trend of monthly sales over a year?
questions.solution: Line charts plot values across a continuous axis - ideal for time-series trends. Pie/doughnut show shares of one whole at a single point; radar compares multiple variables.
questions.shortcut: Trend over time = line, every time.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form of the sentence: 'We should respect our elders.'
questions.solution: **Our elders should be respected** — the modal *should* is kept exactly, be follows it, and the participle closes. 'Should respected' drops be; 'would be respected' swaps the modal itself, which the key never allows.
questions.shortcut: Keep the modal, add be, close with V3.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: **Apply to** an organisation, **apply for** a post. The blank is followed by 'three banks' — organisations — so: **to**. ('He has applied for the clerical post' would use *for*, because a post is the thing requested.)
questions.shortcut: Organisation after the blank → apply to; post → apply for.
questions.passage: Suresh delivers parcels by day and studies for the bank examination by night. He is not ashamed (1) ______ his timetable: thirty minutes of maths on the bus, an hour of English after dinner. His wife manages the accounts of a small jeweller, and the couple rarely watch television (2) ______ Sundays. Suresh has applied (3) ______ three banks so far and keeps a diary of every exam date. His friends laugh at the diary, but he says a man who cannot put (4) ______ small pleasures for a year does not deserve a big one.

questions.q: Select the correct active form of the sentence: 'A new flyover is being built near the market.'
options: They are building a new flyover near the market.
They build a new flyover near the market.
They have built a new flyover near the market.
They were building a new flyover near the market.
questions.solution: is being + V3 is the present continuous row: **They are building a new flyover near the market.** 'Build' drops the continuous; 'have built' jumps to the perfect; 'were building' drifts into the past.
questions.shortcut: being in the passive → V-ing in the active.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The scientist to ___ the award was given belongs to Kerala.
questions.solution: After a preposition, the object form is required: to **whom**. 'To who' is ungrammatical, 'to which' refers to things, and 'whose' needs a following noun.

questions.q: India finished at which position in the Commonwealth Games 2026 medal tally?
questions.solution: India stood 4th with 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze (39 medals), edging host Scotland (also 13 gold, 39 total) on the countback, behind Australia, and the top-2 medal nations.

questions.q: Which of Ashoka's **Major Rock Edicts** describes the Kalinga war and the king's remorse?
questions.solution: **Rock Edict XIII** records the conquest of Kalinga (c. 261 BCE), the deaths and deportations, Ashoka's repentance and his preference for *dhamma-vijaya*. RE II – medical care; RE V – Dhamma Mahamattas; RE XII – religious tolerance.

questions.q: The 18th BRICS Summit (2026) was held at —
questions.solution: India chaired BRICS in 2026 and hosted the 18th Summit on 12 September at **Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi**, with PM Modi, President Xi Jinping and President Putin among the leaders. Rio de Janeiro hosted 2025; Kazan 2024.
questions.shortcut: BRICS ladder: Kazan 2024 → Rio 2025 → New Delhi 2026.

questions.q: Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park in the world, is home to which animal?
questions.solution: **Keibul Lamjao** on **Loktak Lake, Manipur** floats on *phumdis* and protects the endangered **Sangai** (brow-antlered deer). The hangul lives in Dachigam, the Nilgiri tahr in Eravikulam and the one-horned rhino in Kaziranga.

questions.q: For a firm in 2022, income was ₹6.6 crore and expenditure ₹5.5 crore. The profit percentage is:
Find the value of $\sqrt{6 + \sqrt{6 + \sqrt{6 + \cdots \infty}}}$.
questions.solution:
Let $x = \sqrt{6 + \sqrt{6 + \dots}}$. Then $x^2 = 6 + x$, i.e. $x^2 - x - 6 = 0$.
$(x-3)(x+2) = 0$ → $x = 3$ (positive root).
questions.shortcut: Shortcut: 6 = 2 × 3 = k(k+1) with k = 2 → answer k + 1 = 3.

questions.q: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 10% per annum is ₹50. The sum is:
The diagonal of a cuboid of dimensions $3\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}\times12\text{ cm}$ is:
questions.shortcut: $9+16+144=169=13^2$. This cuboid is a stock triplet (3, 4, 12 → 13).

questions.q:
**Statements:** All stones are rocks. All rocks are minerals.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some minerals are stones.
II. All minerals are rocks.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
questions.solution: Stones ⊂ rocks ⊂ minerals, and stones exist, so some minerals are stones → I follows. Minerals extend beyond rocks → II fails. **Only I.**
questions.shortcut: All-chain forward + the free conversion; the chain never runs backwards.

questions.q:
**Statements:** All pens are books. All books are copies.

**Conclusions:** I. All pens are copies. II. Some copies are pens.
questions.solution: pens ⊂ books ⊂ copies gives I. Since pens exist inside copies, II follows too. **Both.**

questions.q: In a certain code language, **'he is kind' is written 'jo ma ne'**; **'she is honest' is written 'ka ma po'**. What is the code for he?
questions.solution: 'is' is common → is = ma. 'He' can be 'jo' or 'ne' → **cannot be determined**.
